risk_management.rationale: Linked by the crosswalk, but 58% of the link weight is on Financial Risk Specialists (13-2054), which O*NET 31.0 has not rated. Analogs: credit analysts and actuaries (quantifying financial risk), financial examiners and compliance managers (checking against rules and limits), management analysts (corporate and operational risk). No adjustments.
risk_management.name: Risk management

fintech_payments.rationale: No ESCO occupation. Payments, fintech and crypto operations combine systems analysis, financial operations management, risk and credit analysis, and quantitative analysis. No adjustment.
fintech_payments.name: Payments, fintech & crypto operations

management_consulting.rationale: Replaces the crosswalk links. The ESCO occupation 'business consultant' (2421.1) crosswalks to Project Management Specialists and Operations Research Analysts, and its other ESCO occupation is unrated, so the linked profile described project management (Freedom to Make Decisions at rank 176 of 205). O*NET's Management Analysts are the consulting occupation; general and operations managers add the client-side change work, and operations research analysts the quantitative strand. No adjustment.
management_consulting.name: Management consulting

independent_advisory.rationale: No ESCO occupation. Independent consulting and interim leadership is management-analyst work plus stepping into general management. Self-employed, so adjusted toward more decision freedom and less structure.
independent_advisory.name: Independent consulting & interim leadership

strategy_games.rationale: Replaces the crosswalk links. Every ESCO occupation assigned to this career path is casino or betting staff (gaming dealer, bingo caller, bookmaker, lottery operator, pit boss), so the linked profile described gambling-floor work, not professional chess or poker players. O*NET has no occupation for professional game players. Analogs: athletes and sports competitors (competitive performance, ranking, self-directed training), coaches (study and analysis of opponents), financial quantitative analysts (probabilistic decision-making) and writers (content and commentary that many professionals live on). No adjustment. The ESCO assignment itself is listed as an open question in REPORT.md.
